title: DTP vaccine (whooping cough, diphtheria, tetanus)
what: A combined vaccine injection that protects against whooping cough, diphtheria and tetanus. Children get several shots on schedule.
why: For children on the national vaccination schedule, and for adults as a booster against diphtheria and tetanus, usually every 10 years.
duration: the shot takes a few seconds; with the check-up usually 15 to 40 minutes
tell_doctor: If your child is sick now or has a fever
Allergies and strong reactions to past vaccines
If there have been seizures or nervous system illness
If your child recently received blood products

prepare.title: Health
prepare.text: The vaccine is given when your child is healthy. Your child will be examined before the shot.

prepare.title: Schedule
prepare.text: Ask your pediatrician for the dates of all the shots in the course.

prepare.title: Fever medicine
prepare.text: Ask the doctor which fever reducer to keep at home in case of a fever.

bring: A favorite toy for your child
steps: The doctor examines your child and takes the temperature
You hold your child in your arms or on your lap
The skin is wiped and the shot is given in the thigh or arm
The vaccine is recorded in the documents
After the shot, stay at the clinic for about 30 minutes
feel: A quick shot. Your child may cry for a bit
Sometimes redness and a firm lump at the spot for 1 to 2 days
after: Stay near the office for 30 minutes
At home offer more drinks and dress your child lightly
red_flags: Trouble breathing, a swollen face, a rash all over: call your local emergency number
Seizures: call your local emergency number
High fever that does not come down, or crying nonstop for several hours: see a doctor urgently

faq.q: Is it true that DTP is a hard vaccine?
faq.a: Reactions are more common than with some others, but they are usually mild and pass in 1 to 3 days.

faq.q: Do adults need a tetanus shot?
faq.a: Yes, a booster is usually given every 10 years. Check with your doctor.

reminders.text: DTP vaccine tomorrow. Bring the vaccination record. Your child should be healthy.
